chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:

I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who hires out his ship and his animal to those who carry wine and pigs in or upon them. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to rent out a ship or animal for carrying wine or pigs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia principle of 'general permissibility' (al-asl fi al--mubaha al-sihha) in commercial contracts, distinguishing between the validity of the lease itself and the specific use of the asset. Scholars note that this ruling applies because the haram items (wine and pigs) are merely cargo, not the object of the sale, thereby avoiding the prohibition of 'selling haram by means of haram' (bay' al-khamr bi al-khamr). It highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams in facilitating daily economic activities while maintaining ritual purity boundaries.
